text:
rex: ap-south1 warm-pool joins are failing, nodes stuck in JOINING for ~15m. batch jobs piling up.
lina: logs show two symptoms: KMS Decrypt AccessDenied and TCP RST to keystore-proxy:443 from bootstrap containers
omar: did anyone touch firewall rules or privnet egress in that region last night?
sophia: eng-security pushed egress-hardening v1.3 to ap-south1 ~02:30Z which added a default deny for outbound 0.0.0.0/0 except keystore-aggregator IPs. looks like aggregator IPs rotated during failover and are no longer in allowlist
rex: aha. bootstrap uses keystore-proxy DNS that resolves to aggregator IPv6+IPv4 LB. if LB IP changed, firewall blocks egress -> bootstrap falls back to local caching layer which tries KMS with SourceIp condition, failing with mismatch
sec-bot: policy-deploy egress-hardening v1.3 -> ap-south1 at 2026-03-24T02:31Z; contact=eng-security
lina: sample bootstrap tail: ```Mar 24 03:18:12 bootstrap decrypt failed: AccessDenied KMS:Decrypt Condition aws:SourceIp != expected; Mar 24 03:18:12 network: connect keystore-proxy:443 -> RST```
omar: options: (1) temporarily add current aggregator LB IPs to egress allowlist for ap-south1, (2) open keystore-proxy DNS name (SNI) outbound via L7 proxy, (3) fallback to rolling rollback of egress-hardening v1.3.
sophia: prefer 1 with tight TTL. adding LB IPs costs nothing but must be reversible. we also need to add automation to sync aggregator IP changes into firewall rules to avoid recurrence
rex: production impact: warm-pool down -> we spawn on-demand GPUs. rough incremental spend ~ $6k/day if continues through peak window
lina: security considerations: adding IPs is low blast but LB IPs are ephemeral; must set 30m TTL and enable ip-change alerts. also log all decrypt calls during window.
sec-bot: eng-security emergency approval required for allowlist exception. please post exact IPs and TTL in this thread for audit.
omar: current public LB IPs resolved from keystore-proxy.ap-svc.redwood.internal: 52.62.11.204, 52.62.11.205, 2001:db8:abcd::1
rex: applying temporary allowlist for those three addresses with TTL 30m, revert job scheduled. also enabling packet capture for first 20 bootstraps. snippet of iptables change we will push to egress fw-asg:
```bash
# allow keystore aggregator for bootstrap window
iptables -I OUTPUT -d 52.62.11.204 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
iptables -I OUTPUT -d 52.62.11.205 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
ip -6 neigh add 2001:db8:abcd::1 dev eth0
```
sophia: make sure to record a ticket in eng-security channel and create an audit tag on the bootstrap requests: `x-rls-temp: warmpool-unblock-20260324` so we can find events easily
infra-bot: incident INC-20260324-warmpool-egress created, assignees=eng-ml,eng-security, status=investigating
sec-bot: emergency exception granted: allowlist for 52.62.11.204/205 and 2001:db8:abcd::1 for 30m. condition: request header x-rls-temp=warmpool-unblock-20260324. revert job scheduled.
lina: applying commits to firewall-asg now, will follow with canary 3 joins
rex: canary 1 succeeded (node -> Ready). canary 2/3 in progress
sophia: seeing decrypt successes in audit logs with `x-rls-temp` header present. no anomalous requests flagged by SIEM so far
omar: after full canary, follow-ups: (A) implement DNS-to-IP sync for allowlist, (B) update keystore aggregator to advertise stable private IPs for regional bootstraps, (C) add integration test that simulates LB IP rotation during egress-hardening rollout
rex: agreed. will create infra-PRs and schedule postmortem. leaving incident open until follow-ups tracked
infra-bot: INC-20260324-warmpool-egress status=mitigated followup=postmortem-20260325
